record.paper_title: Open Questions Related to Bose-Einstein Correlations in e+e− → Hadrons
record.context_brief: decrease of BEC/FDC emitter radius with hadron mass
record.original_question: In hadronic Z⁰ decays studied with Bose-Einstein correlations for identical boson pairs and Fermi-Dirac correlations for baryon pairs, what hadronization explanation can account for the observed decrease of the emitter dimension r(m) with hadron mass, from about 0.75 fm at the pion mass to about 0.15 fm at the Lambda-baryon mass, especially given that many hadronization models, including the Lund model, expect r to increase with hadron mass and that the very small Lambda emitter dimension lacks a satisfactory explanation?

evidence.quote: The very high statistics of the Z0 hadronic decay events accumulated by the LEP experiments and the extension of the BEC analysis to baryon pairs via the FDC method opened the way to study the emitter dimension rππ as a function of the hadron mass, from pions to Λ baryons.
The emitter dimension r(m) is seen to decrease with the hadron mass, from ∼0.75 fm at mπ to ∼0.15 fm at mΛ.

On the other hand, the decrease of r with the hadron mass poses a challenge to a large variety of hadronisation models, including the Lund one, which expect r to increase with the hadron mass. In particular at present, there is no satisfactory explanation for the very small rΛ value.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In high-energy e⁺e⁻ annihilation at the Z⁰ resonance, identical-boson pairs (e.g. ππ, KK) exhibit Bose–Einstein correlations (BEC) and identical-baryon pairs (e.g. ΛΛ) exhibit Fermi–Dirac correlations (FDC). From these correlations one extracts an emitter (source) dimension r(m) of the production region for each species of mass m, conventionally by fitting the two-particle correlation function C(Q) (Q being the four-momentum difference) with a Goldhaber-type parametrization C(Q) = 1 ± λ exp(−r²Q²). Experimental measurements yield the hierarchy r(mπ) ≈ 0.75 fm, r(mK) intermediate, and r(mΛ) ≈ 0.15 fm, so r(m) decreases with increasing hadron mass.

Many widely used hadronization frameworks, including the Lund string model, instead predict that r should grow (or at least not decrease) with the hadron mass. Provide a hadronization-level explanation that:
(a) accounts quantitatively for the observed monotone decrease r(m) of the emitter dimension from the pion to the Λ baryon, and
(b) explains, in particular, the very small value r(mΛ) ≈ 0.15 fm,
within (or as a justified modification of) a string/cluster-type hadronization picture, beyond a purely kinematical Heisenberg-uncertainty appeal.
artifact.category_tag: Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac correlations in hadronization
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that the observed decrease r(m) ∝ 1/m can be heuristically described via the Heisenberg uncertainty principle and general QCD potential considerations, but standard hadronization models (Lund string, cluster) still predict the opposite trend, and no satisfactory hadronization-level explanation for the very small Λ emitter radius has been established. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Emitter size as a function of mass and transverse mass
status_evidence.snippet: r is found to be proportional to 1/m and can be described in terms of the Heisenberg uncertainty relations and general QCD potential considerations.
status_evidence.claim: A kinematical/QCD-potential description of r(m) ∝ 1/m exists, but this is not a hadronization-model derivation.

status_evidence.title: Mass and transverse mass effects on the hadron emitter size
status_evidence.snippet: Hierarchy rππ>rKK>rΛΛ observed in Z0 hadronic decays.
status_evidence.claim: The experimental hierarchy is confirmed, contradicting Lund-type expectations.

status_evidence.title: Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac correlations: Measurements versus Monte Carlo
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of implementation of BEC/FDC effects in MC simulations and remaining discrepancies.
status_evidence.claim: Existing hadronization Monte Carlos do not naturally reproduce the decrease of r with hadron mass.
